text:
Marathon Petroleum shares jumped 6.25% today as crude oil prices surged more than 4% on geopolitical tensions in the Middle East. A report that the U.S. is sending a third aircraft carrier strike group to the region, combined with concerns over Iran's role in a British air base incident, drove Brent crude sharply higher—a direct tailwind for refiners, whose profits depend on the spread between oil input costs and refined product prices. Refinery utilization is already running at 92.5%, so the company is well-positioned to capture gains from higher margins.

The broader energy market is also tightening heading into winter, with reports of Europe facing a potential energy crunch and BP announcing a major oil discovery. Higher crude prices flowing through a fully-utilized refinery network typically translate into stronger refining margins, which explains the sharp single-day move in a stock that had been essentially flat over the prior two weeks.
